name: Dust Collapse to Black Holes in Anti-de Sitter Space
description: A cloud of pressureless dust collapsing under a negative cosmological constant, joined across its surface to a static black hole. In three dimensions a disc of dust dense enough makes the black hole of Bañados, Teitelboim, and Zanelli, and in four a slab of dust with hyperbolic or flat faces makes a black hole whose horizon is a surface of higher genus or a torus.
convention: The cosmological constant is $\Lambda = -1/\ell^2$ in three dimensions and $\Lambda = -3/L^2$ in four, and the dust is released from rest with density $\rho_0$ where its scale factor is $a = 1$. We keep factors of $c$ explicit, with $G_3$ Newton's constant in three dimensions and $G$ the constant of four.
history: Release a disc of dust from rest in three spacetime dimensions, with no cosmological constant, and it stays as it is [mann1993]. Matter there curves spacetime only where it sits, and in the words of Steven Giddings, James Abbott, and Karel Kuchař, "a dust distribution moves without any geodesic deviation between the particles" [giddings1984]. Máximo Bañados, Claudio Teitelboim, and Jorge Zanelli found in 1992 that a negative cosmological constant, $\Lambda = -1/\ell^2$, permits a black hole in those dimensions [banados1992]. In August of that year Robert Mann and Simon Ross, at the University of Waterloo, asked when a disc of dust, "the 3D analog of Oppenheimer-Snyder collapse", ends as that black hole [mann1993]. J. Robert Oppenheimer and Hartland Snyder had solved the collapse of a star without pressure in 1939: its matter reaches the centre in a finite proper time, and an observer outside sees it shrink toward its gravitational radius as its light reddens [oppenheimersnyder1939].¶Inside the dust Mann and Ross took the metric of a homogeneous universe, $$ds^2 = -c^2dt^2 + a(t)^2\left(\frac{dr^2}{1 - kr^2} + r^2d\theta^2\right),$$ and outside it the black hole without rotation, with metric function $R^2/\ell^2 - M$ [mann1993]. The field equations reduce to $d^2a/dt^2 = -c^2a/\ell^2$, in which the density is absent, so a disc released from rest shrinks as $a = \cos(ct/\ell)$ and reaches zero size after the proper time $\pi\ell/(2c)$, whatever its density and radius [mann1993]. Mann and Ross required the metric and the extrinsic curvature to be continuous across the edge $r = r_0$, and obtained $M = 8\pi G_3\rho_0r_0^2/c^2 - 1$, with $G_3$ Newton's constant in three dimensions, so the density at release, $\rho_0$, sets the mass seen from outside [mann1993]. For $M > 0$ the edge crosses a horizon at $R = \ell\sqrt{M}$ in a finite proper time, and the disc ends as the black hole of Bañados, Teitelboim, and Zanelli; with less matter the endpoint is "a naked conical singularity in anti-deSitter space" [mann1993]. To an observer outside, the edge takes an infinite time to reach the horizon and its light reddens without limit, as with Oppenheimer and Snyder's star [mann1993]. Steven Carlip likened the threshold in 1995 to the transition that Matthew Choptuik had found numerically in four dimensions [carlip1995].¶Yoav Peleg and Alan Steif replaced the disc by a thin ring of dust in 1995 and found an order parameter built from the mass that vanishes at the threshold as the square root of the distance from it [peleg1995]. A massless scalar field ended the same way when Frans Pretorius and Choptuik collapsed it numerically in 2000: outside the horizon the geometry approached the same black hole, and a spacelike curvature singularity grew inside [pretorius2000]. Sashideep Gutti gave the dust an uneven density in 2005 and found that the singularity is covered only if the mass of the outermost shell exceeds a critical value [gutti2005]. Cenalo Vaz, Gutti, Claus Kiefer, and Tejinder Pal Singh quantized the collapsing dust in 2007 and derived Hawking radiation from the black holes it forms [vaz2007]. Vaz and K. R. Koehler set the dust rotating in 2008 and joined it to the spinning black hole, and in their solutions no singularity forms [vaz2008]. Zijian Shi and Xiangdong Zhang gave the disc the modified Friedmann equation of loop quantum cosmology in 2026, and found outside it a hole with two horizons, joined through a transition region to a white hole [shi2026].¶Stefan Åminneborg, Ingemar Bengtsson, Sören Holst, and Peter Peldán identified points of anti-de Sitter space in four dimensions in 1996 and obtained black holes whose horizons are tori or surfaces of higher genus, and Mann gave such holes mass and charge [aminneborg1996, mann1997]. W. L. Smith and Mann showed in 1997 that a cloud of dust collapses to them [smith1997]. Inside the cloud the metric is $$ds^2 = -c^2dt^2 + a(t)^2\left(\frac{dr^2}{r^2/b^2 - 1} + r^2\left(d\theta^2 + \sinh^2\theta\,d\phi^2\right)\right),$$ a universe of spatial curvature $-1/b^2$ sliced by hyperbolic planes, and outside it the metric function is $-1 - \mu/R + R^2/L^2$, with $\Lambda = -3/L^2$ [smith1997, mena2008toroidal]. Joining the two across $r = r_0$, they obtained $\mu = 8\pi G\rho_0r_0^3/(3c^2)$ for a cloud released at $a = 1$, so any density makes a hole, and concluded that "black holes with event horizons of any topology can form from the collapse of such a cloud" [smith1997]. A cloud at rest falls only if $8\pi G\rho_0/c^2 < 3/L^2$: a greater density would turn the curvature of its space positive [smith1997]. With no dust the interior is anti-de Sitter space, and its scale factor vanishes where the surfaces of identification meet [smith1997].¶José Lemos proposed a collapse to the flat holes, whose horizons are planes, cylinders, or tori, in 1998: in that model matter with the topology of a torus falls to a toroidal black hole as it absorbs radiation from outside [lemos1998]. Filipe Mena, José Natário, and Paul Tod showed in 2008 that a spatially flat universe of dust cannot be joined to the static flat hole [mena2008toroidal]. The open universe can, when its space is sliced by horospheres, $a(t)^2\left(d\chi^2 + e^{2\chi/b}(dx^2 + dy^2)\right)$, a case Smith and Mann had mentioned and left undone [mena2008toroidal, smith1997]. Mena and João Oliveira proved in 2017 that the flat universe cannot be joined to a radiating flat exterior either, when its surface starts untrapped [mena2017]. The hyperbolic cloud is a slab: its surfaces shrink to a smallest one at $r = b$ and grow again to a second face, so the whole is a wormhole between two black holes, which causal curves cannot cross from one infinity to the other [mena2010]. The flat cloud narrows without end toward a cusp at infinite distance and stays noncompact when its faces are closed into tori [mena2008toroidal, mena2010].¶Mann found in 1997 that a region of negative energy density can collapse to a black hole of negative mass and nontrivial topology [mann1997negative]. Smith and Mann found in 1998 that a static star of constant density with a flat or hyperbolic surface is a wormhole too where its pressure and density are regular, made of matter that violates the weak energy condition [smith1998]. Lemos sent shells of radiation into anti-de Sitter space in 1999: with a toroidal, cylindrical, or planar front they form black holes and no naked singularity, in accord with cosmic censorship and against the hoop conjecture [lemos1999]. Mena, Natário, and Tod joined dust of uneven density, from the Szekeres and Lemaître-Tolman families, to the flat and hyperbolic holes, and then extended the construction to higher dimensions [mena2008toroidal, mena2010]. Mena and Oliveira gave the cloud pressure and a radiating exterior, and obtained a dynamical horizon of higher genus [mena2017].

related.text: The outside of the collapsing disc. Its edge falls along a radial geodesic of the hole without rotation, whose mass is $M = 8\pi G_3\rho_0r_0^2/c^2 - 1$ [mann1993].
The outside of the clouds of four dimensions: the hyperbolic hole for a cloud sliced by hyperbolic planes, and the flat hole for a cloud sliced by horospheres [smith1997, mena2008toroidal].
The inside of the clouds of four dimensions, a slab cut from an open Friedmann universe of dust with a negative cosmological constant [smith1997, mena2008toroidal].

The star without pressure that J. Robert Oppenheimer and Hartland Snyder let fall in 1939, in four dimensions with no cosmological constant. Robert Mann and Simon Ross called their disc "the 3D analog of Oppenheimer-Snyder collapse" [oppenheimersnyder1939, mann1993].
With no dust, $\rho_0 = 0$, the hyperbolic cloud is anti-de Sitter space, and its scale factor vanishes where the surfaces of identification meet [smith1997].
The black hole of anti-de Sitter space with a round horizon. These clouds end as its counterparts whose horizons are tori or surfaces of higher genus [smith1997].
A disc too light to make a horizon ends as a conical singularity, the point mass of three dimensions, here in anti-de Sitter space [mann1993].

Oppenheimer and Snyder's star with the bounce of loop quantum cosmology inside it. Zijian Shi and Xiangdong Zhang gave the disc of three dimensions a modified Friedmann equation of the same kind in 2026 [shi2026].
Dust with no symmetry required of it. Filipe Mena, José Natário, and Paul Tod joined its members with flat and with hyperbolic shells to the black holes these clouds make [mena2008toroidal].
The collapse with the dust on one thin shell. Yoav Peleg and Alan Steif let a ring of dust fall in three dimensions, with and without a cosmological constant [peleg1995].

coordinates.name: Comoving Disc of Dust

parameters.description: Scale factor of the dust, a pure number, $a = \cos(ct/\ell)$ for a disc released from rest at $t = 0$, which solves $\ddot{a} = -a/\ell^2$
Curvature of the disc's space at release, of either sign, $k = 8\pi G_3\rho_0/c^2 - 1/\ell^2$
Comoving radius of the edge of the disc, a length, with $r_0 < 1/\sqrt{k}$ where $k > 0$
Anti-de Sitter radius, a length, fixed by the cosmological constant through $\Lambda = -1/\ell^2$

coordinates.convention: We use Mann and Ross's comoving coordinates $(t, r, \theta)$, with $t$ the proper time of the dust and $r$ a length, and the disc is $r \le r_0$. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, a dot on the scale factor is $\dot{a} = \dfrac{1}{c}\dfrac{da}{dt}$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.

coordinates.name: Static Exterior of the Disc

parameters.description: Anti-de Sitter radius, a length, fixed by the cosmological constant through $\Lambda = -1/\ell^2$
Mass of the hole, dimensionless, $M = 8\pi G_3\rho_0r_0^2/c^2 - 1$ for a disc whose edge is released at the radius $r_0$; a horizon forms only for $M > 0$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(T, R, \theta)$ outside the disc, with $T$ carrying dimensions of time and $T = 0$ at the moment of rest, and the edge of the disc is at $R = R_s(T)$, with $R_s = r_0a$ for the scale factor $a$ of the dust. We take components in the chart $x^0 = cT$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{T}$ means $d(cT)/d\lambda$.

coordinates.name: Ingoing Exterior of the Disc

parameters.description: Anti-de Sitter radius, a length, fixed by the cosmological constant through $\Lambda = -1/\ell^2$
Mass of the hole, dimensionless, $M = 8\pi G_3\rho_0r_0^2/c^2 - 1$ for a disc whose edge is released at the radius $r_0$; a horizon forms only for $M > 0$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(v, R, \theta)$ outside the disc, with the advanced time $v$ a length, $dv = c\,dT + dR/\left(R^2/\ell^2 - M\right)$, and the edge of the disc is at $R = R_s(v)$, with $R_s = r_0a$ for the scale factor $a$ of the dust. A dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter.

coordinates.name: Comoving Hyperbolic Cloud

parameters.description: Scale factor of the dust, a pure number with $a = 1$ at release, which solves $\dot{a}^2 = 1/b^2 + \left(1/L^2 - 1/b^2\right)/a - a^2/L^2$
Curvature radius of the cloud's space at release, a length greater than $L$, fixed by the density through $1/b^2 = 1/L^2 - 8\pi G\rho_0/(3c^2)$
Comoving radius of a face of the cloud, a length greater than $b$
Anti-de Sitter radius, a length, with $\Lambda = -3/L^2$

coordinates.convention: We use Smith and Mann's comoving coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, with $t$ the proper time of the dust and $r$ a length, between the smallest surface of the cloud, $r = b$, and a face, $r = r_0$, and the scale factor reaches zero at $t = t_c$. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, a dot on the scale factor is $\dot{a} = \dfrac{1}{c}\dfrac{da}{dt}$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.

coordinates.name: Hyperbolic Cloud between Its Faces

parameters.description: Scale factor of the dust, a pure number with $a = 1$ at release, which solves $\dot{a}^2 = 1/b^2 + \left(1/L^2 - 1/b^2\right)/a - a^2/L^2$
Curvature radius of the cloud's space at release, a length greater than $L$, fixed by the density through $1/b^2 = 1/L^2 - 8\pi G\rho_0/(3c^2)$
Comoving distance of each face from the smallest surface, a length, where the radius of the face is $r_0 = b\cosh(\chi_0/b)$
Anti-de Sitter radius, a length, with $\Lambda = -3/L^2$

coordinates.convention: We use comoving coordinates $(t, \chi, \theta, \phi)$, with $t$ the proper time of the dust and $\chi$ the distance at release from the smallest surface of the cloud, where Smith and Mann's radius is $r = b\cosh(\chi/b)$, and the scale factor reaches zero at $t = t_c$. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, a dot on the scale factor is $\dot{a} = \dfrac{1}{c}\dfrac{da}{dt}$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.

coordinates.name: Static Exterior of the Hyperbolic Cloud

parameters.description: Mass parameter, a length, $\mu = 8\pi G\rho_0r_0^3/(3c^2)$ for a cloud whose face is released at the radius $r_0$
Anti-de Sitter radius, a length, with $\Lambda = -3/L^2$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(T, R, \theta, \phi)$ outside a face of the cloud, with $T$ carrying dimensions of time and $T = 0$ at the moment of rest, and the face is at $R = R_s(T)$, with $R_s = r_0a$ for the scale factor $a$ of the dust. The horizon $R_h$ is the positive root of $-1 - \mu/R + R^2/L^2$. We take components in the chart $x^0 = cT$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{T}$ means $d(cT)/d\lambda$.
geodesics: \ddot{R} + \dfrac{\left(2R^3 + L^2\,\mu\right)\left(R^3 - L^2\,R - L^2\,\mu\right)}{2L^4\,R^3}\dot{T}^2 - \dfrac{2R^3 + L^2\,\mu}{2R\left(R^3 - L^2\,R - L^2\,\mu\right)}\dot{R}^2 - \dfrac{R^3 - L^2\,R - L^2\,\mu}{L^2}\dot{\theta}^2 - \dfrac{\left(R^3 - L^2\,R - L^2\,\mu\right)\sinh^2\theta}{L^2}\dot{\phi}^2 = 0

coordinates.name: Comoving Flat Cloud

parameters.description: Scale factor of the dust, a pure number with $a = 1$ at release, which solves $\dot{a}^2 = 1/b^2 + \left(1/L^2 - 1/b^2\right)/a - a^2/L^2$
Curvature radius of the cloud's space at release, a length greater than $L$, fixed by the density through $1/b^2 = 1/L^2 - 8\pi G\rho_0/(3c^2)$
Comoving position of the face of the cloud, a length, where the radius of the face at release is $R_0 = be^{\chi_0/b}$
Anti-de Sitter radius, a length, with $\Lambda = -3/L^2$

coordinates.convention: We use comoving coordinates $(t, \chi, x, y)$, with $t$ the proper time of the dust and $\chi$, $x$, and $y$ lengths, and the cloud is $\chi \le \chi_0$, with the scale factor reaching zero at $t = t_c$. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, a dot on the scale factor is $\dot{a} = \dfrac{1}{c}\dfrac{da}{dt}$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.

coordinates.name: Static Exterior of the Flat Cloud

parameters.description: Mass parameter, a length, $\mu = 8\pi G\rho_0R_0^3/(3c^2)$ for a cloud whose face is released at the radius $R_0$
Anti-de Sitter radius, a length, with $\Lambda = -3/L^2$
Curvature radius of the cloud's space at release, a length, the scale of $x$ and $y$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(T, R, x, y)$ outside the face of the cloud, with $T$ carrying dimensions of time, $T = 0$ at the moment of rest, and $x$ and $y$ the lengths of the cloud's comoving coordinates, and the face is at $R = R_s(T)$, with $R_s = R_0a$ for the scale factor $a$ of the dust. We take components in the chart $x^0 = cT$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{T}$ means $d(cT)/d\lambda$.
geodesics: \ddot{R} + \dfrac{\left(R^3 - L^2\,\mu\right)\left(2R^3 + L^2\,\mu\right)}{2L^4\,R^3}\dot{T}^2 - \dfrac{2R^3 + L^2\,\mu}{2R\left(R^3 - L^2\,\mu\right)}\dot{R}^2 - \dfrac{R^3 - L^2\,\mu}{L^2\,b^2}\dot{x}^2 - \dfrac{R^3 - L^2\,\mu}{L^2\,b^2}\dot{y}^2 = 0
